transcript.text: Bosch KGN34NL3AG - some days it's fine, other days it just clicks every few minutes at the back and doesn't seem to run, and the freezer starts getting soft. Then it starts working again by itself. What's going on?

That is not normal defrost behaviour. A click every few minutes from the lower rear of the fridge, combined with the freezer warming, usually means the compressor is attempting to start, failing, then its protection device resets and tries again.

Most likely causes, in roughly this order:

• Faulty compressor start device / PTC relay / overload protector (on conventional fixed-speed compressors)
• Faulty inverter/control module (if this model has an inverter-driven compressor)
• Compressor becoming difficult to start or failing internally — more expensive possibility
• Less commonly: poor mains supply/loose plug, overheated compressor due to poor ventilation or heavy dust, or a control-board fault

When it later works again, the compressor may have cooled down enough for its thermal protector to reset, or the failing start/control component happens to work temporarily.

### What to check safely
1. Listen at the bottom back: after a click, does the black compressor hum briefly for a few seconds, then click off? That strongly supports a start/compressor fault.
2. Feel carefully near the compressor: if it is extremely hot while it is repeatedly clicking, stop trying to make it run. Heat is consistent with repeated failed starts.
3. Make sure there is ventilation around the rear/sides and that the condenser area is not heavily dust-covered.
4. Plug it directly into a wall socket, not a loose extension lead or multiway adaptor.
5. You can switch it off at the wall for 10–15 minutes and restart it once. If it returns to click–pause–click behaviour, don’t keep cycling it repeatedly.

### What to do next
Arrange an appliance engineer/Bosch service visit and describe it as:

> “Intermittent compressor start failure: clicking from the rear every few minutes, no compressor running, freezer temperature rising; then it recovers by itself.”

They should test the compressor start circuit/inverter and compressor current draw, rather than merely replacing a thermostat.

If it is a bad relay or inverter module, repair can be reasonable. If the compressor itself is failing, the repair may be less economical, especially outside warranty.

### Food safety
Move valuable frozen food elsewhere if you can. Food that is still hard-frozen or still contains ice crystals can generally be refrozen, although quality may suffer. Fully thawed perishable food should not be left warm for long; when in doubt, discard it.

Because the freezer is already softening, I would treat this as an urgent fault rather than wait to see whether it settles.

Thank you. To answer your points: after the click there is a very brief hum and then silence for a few minutes before the next click. The box on the side of the compressor is very hot to touch when this happens. The back is a bit dusty but there is a gap around it, and it is plugged straight into a wall socket. I get the same on another socket. There is no burning smell and nothing has tripped. I haven't tried switching it off for 10-15 minutes, so should I do that before booking an engineer?

Yes — one controlled power-off test is reasonable before booking, but it is unlikely to be a permanent cure.

Your description is very characteristic of a compressor start problem:

• click
• very brief hum
• click/silence for several minutes
• very hot box on the compressor
• eventually it may start again after cooling down

The hot box is likely the compressor’s start/overload device or, depending on the compressor type, its electronic drive module. It is cutting out to protect the compressor after a failed start attempt.

### Try this once
1. Switch the fridge off at the wall and unplug it.
2. Leave it off for at least 20–30 minutes — 10 minutes may not be long enough for the hot protector/module to cool.
3. Keep the doors shut while it is off.
4. Plug it directly back into the wall socket and turn it on.
5. Listen for the compressor over the next 10–20 minutes.

If it starts and then runs continuously with a normal low hum, it may cool again for a while. But that does not prove it is fixed; intermittent start relays/modules and failing compressors can behave normally after cooling, then fail again later.

If it goes back to the brief hum/click cycle, or the compressor-side box becomes too hot to comfortably touch, switch it off and arrange service rather than leaving it to keep attempting starts for hours.

### Booking an engineer
I would still book one, especially because the freezer has already softened. Tell them:

> “The compressor makes a brief hum after a click, then cuts out and retries every few minutes. The start/control box on the side of the compressor becomes very hot, and the freezer warms. It works again intermittently after being left.”

That directs them toward checking the compressor starting electronics/overload device and compressor condition.

### Food
If the freezer contents are becoming soft, move valuable food to another freezer/cool box as soon as possible. Food that is still properly frozen with ice crystals can generally be refrozen, but fully thawed food should be treated according to normal food-safety guidance and not simply left in the unreliable freezer.

Thank you, I'll try the 20-30 minute power-off test once and see what happens. If it goes back to clicking, I'll book an engineer and use the wording you gave me. Is there anything else I should tell them, such as the model number KGN34NL3AG?
